title: gswp-1999-world-heavyweight
label: Fang

won.source: Billed as the reigning champion entering the promotion's own 2 May and 13 June 1999 broadcasts, following an April 1999 single-elimination tournament for the then-vacant title; the tournament final is not in the read record.

lost.note: Lost to Johnny Glamour at Summer Showdown after a returning ally, King Snake, struck him with a chair and a third wrestler's rescue attempt arrived a beat too late.

note: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing rather than a surviving title-change document.

title: gswp-1999-television
label: "Ice Storm" Chris Winters

won.source: Billed as the reigning Television Champion, not defending the title, on the promotion's own 30 May 1999 broadcast, and again at its 13 June 1999 Pay-Per-View, where he retained it in a four-way defense; how or when he won it is not stated in the read record.

note: Retained the title in further defenses on 20 and 28 June and 11 July 1999, the last of which survives as its own document.

title: gswp-1999-television
label: Boltz

won.source: Defeated "True Playa" Mike Wilson for the title on the promotion's own 2 May 1999 broadcast.

lost.note: Not attested in the read record; "Ice Storm" Chris Winters is already billed as the reigning, non-defending Television Champion by the promotion's own 30 May 1999 broadcast.

note: Recorded from the promotion's own repeated billing rather than a surviving title-change document.

won.source: Billed as the promotion's own former Television Champion at its 13 June 1999 Pay-Per-View; the reign itself predates the read record.

lost.note: Lost the title to Boltz on the promotion's own 2 May 1999 broadcast.

title: gswp-1999-extreme

won.source: Named as one of three entrants in the promotion's own three-way "dance to the death" announced on 2 May 1999 to crown the first champion; the match itself is not in the read record, and he is billed as reigning champion by the promotion's own 13 June 1999 Pay-Per-View.
